articles.title: Segundo turno em Minas Gerais: veja balanço | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente reeleito venceu por uma diferença de pouco mais de 109 mil votos no estado. Dia da votação também foi marcado por chuvas intensas, substituição de urnas e prorrogação do horário de votação.
articles.summary: O segundo turno em Minas Gerais teve vitória de Lula sobre Flávio Bolsonaro, queda na abstenção e 212 denúncias de assédio eleitoral no ambiente de trabalho.
articles.body:
Segundo turno das eleições em Minas Gerais: veja imagens do domingo de votação em BH — Foto: Fernanda Torquato/TV Globo

O segundo turno das eleições de 2026, realizado no último domingo (25), foi marcado pela virada do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) sobre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em Minas Gerais, pela redução da abstenção e por ocorrências relacionadas às fortes chuvas que atingiram parte do estado.

Lula recebeu 50,43% (6.351.099) dos votos válidos em Minas, contra 49,57% (6.241.786) de Flávio Bolsonaro. A diferença foi de 109.313 votos . Mais de 13 milhões de mineiros compareceram às urnas, enquanto cerca de 3,3 milhões deixaram de votar.

Confira abaixo os principais acontecimentos do segundo turno em Minas Gerais a partir dos tópicos abaixo:

Apoiadores de Lula comemoram reeleição em Belo Horizonte

Como votaram as maiores cidades do estado

Funcionamento das urnas e ocorrências eleitorais

Minas é o segundo estado com mais denúncias de assédio eleitoral

Eleitora registra comemoração na Praça Sete, em Belo Horizonte — Foto: Fernanda Torquato

Minas Gerais foi o único estado brasileiro em que a liderança na disputa presidencial mudou entre o primeiro e o segundo turno. No dia 4 de outubro, Flávio Bolsonaro havia recebido 48,24% dos votos válidos no estado, contra 43,33% de Lula.

Três semanas depois, o presidente reverteu a desvantagem e venceu com 6.351.099 votos , diante de 6.241.786 do adversário. Entre os dois turnos, Lula conquistou mais de 1,1 milhão de votos adicionais, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro ampliou sua votação em cerca de 464 mil votos.

Criança acompanha comemoração na Praça Sete, em Belo Horizonte — Foto: Fernanda Torquato

A reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) levou apoiadores às ruas de Belo Horizonte na noite de domingo.

A comemoração se concentrou principalmente na Rua Sapucaí, no bairro Floresta , na Região Leste da capital, onde uma multidão se reuniu com bandeiras, roupas vermelhas e instrumentos musicais.

A festa também se espalhou por outros pontos da cidade, como a Praça Sete e o Viaduto de Santa Tereza. Houve buzinaços, música e manifestações de apoio ao presidente reeleito. As celebrações ocorreram apesar de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ter vencido a disputa na capital mineira, com 50,80% dos votos válidos, contra 49,20% de Lula.

Apesar da vitória de Lula no estado, Flávio Bolsonaro foi o mais votado em oito das dez maiores cidades mineiras : Belo Horizonte, Uberlândia, Contagem, Betim, Montes Claros, Uberaba, Governador Valadares e Ipatinga.

Lula venceu em Juiz de Fora, na Zona da Mata, com 57,66% dos votos válidos, e em Ribeirão das Neves, na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, com 52,27%.

Na capital, Flávio Bolsonaro teve 50,80%, contra 49,20% de Lula. A vantagem do candidato do PL, no entanto, caiu de quase 99 mil votos no primeiro turno para pouco mais de 24 mil no segundo.

Eleitores votam na Escola Estadual Governador Milton Campos, conhecida como Estadual Central, em Belo Horizonte — Foto: Fernanda Torquato

A abstenção eleitoral em Minas Gerais caiu 10,9% entre os dois turnos , segundo dados da Justiça Eleitoral. O número de eleitores que não compareceram passou de 3.735.098, no primeiro turno, para 3.327.941, no segundo, uma redução de 407.157 ausentes.

Em termos percentuais, a abstenção passou de 22,81% para 20,33%. Especialistas ouvidos pela TV Globo apontaram a mobilização de jovens e de eleitores mais velhos, além do engajamento político nas redes sociais, como possíveis fatores para o aumento da participação.

Mulher dentro de seção da Escola Estadual Laura das Chagas Ferreira, no Aglomerado da Serra — Foto: Fernanda Torquato

O Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Minas Gerais (TRE-MG) avaliou como tranquila a votação do segundo turno no estado . Ao todo, 140 urnas eletrônicas precisaram ser substituídas, o equivalente a 0,27% das 52.062 seções eleitorais. No primeiro turno, foram 171 substituições.

A Justiça Eleitoral também registrou 127 ocorrências de segurança até as 21h de domingo, principalmente por tentativa de violação do sigilo do voto e propaganda irregular de boca de urna. Ao todo, 52 pessoas foram conduzidas às delegacias. No primeiro turno, haviam sido contabilizadas 408 ocorrências.

Eleitores chegam ao Colégio Sagrada Família — Foto: Fernanda Torquato

A decisão do ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), de estender a votação até as 19h chegou quando diversas seções eleitorais de Minas Gerais já haviam encerrado os trabalhos.

Em escolas de Belo Horizonte, Contagem e Ribeirão das Neves, urnas foram lacradas e boletins de votação emitidos antes da comunicação sobre a prorrogação . Entre os locais estavam escolas dos bairros Camargos e Barreiro, na capital.

O TRE-MG informou que recebeu a orientação por volta das 18h e determinou a continuidade da votação nas seções que ainda estivessem abertas. A medida foi adotada após relatos de dificuldades no transporte de eleitores.

Eleitores na Escola Municipal Santos Dumont, em BH — Foto: Fernanda Torquato/TV Globo

Um levantamento divulgado pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) na terça-feira (27) apontou que Minas Gerais registrou 2.253 votos após as 17h no segundo turno . Todos foram computados entre 17h e 18h.

Em todo o país, foram contabilizados 34.393 votos depois do horário inicialmente previsto para o encerramento da votação. A prorrogação foi determinada pelo STF para seções que permaneciam abertas, diante de dificuldades relatadas pelas candidaturas à Presidência da República.

Minas é o 2º estado em denúncias de assédio eleitoral

Eleitores comparecem à Escola Estadual Santos Dumont, em Belo Horizonte, para votar no segundo turno das eleições — Foto: Fernanda Torquato

Minas Gerais terminou as eleições de 2026 como o segundo estado com mais denúncias de assédio eleitoral no ambiente de trabalho , segundo o Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT).

Até o encerramento do segundo turno, o órgão havia recebido 212 denúncias no estado, contra 110 registradas até o primeiro turno. Em todo o Brasil, foram 1.939 registros.

As denúncias envolvem possíveis pressões, constrangimentos e tentativas de influenciar a escolha política de trabalhadores. Entre os casos investigados em Minas estão situações envolvendo empresas de Belo Horizonte e Bom Despacho, no Centro-Oeste do estado.

Cartaz aponta seções que mudaram de sala devido à chuva na Escola Estadual Carlos Drummond, no bairro Floramar, em Belo Horizonte, neste domingo (25) de eleição — Foto: Cláudia Mourão/TV Globo

O segundo turno também foi marcado por fortes chuvas em Belo Horizonte e na Região Metropolitana. Na tarde de domingo, a Defesa Civil da capital emitiu dois alertas severos para a população.

O primeiro aviso, enviado às 12h57, alertava para o risco de enxurradas e alagamentos. Às 13h10, um segundo comunicado informou sobre a possibilidade de granizo nas duas horas seguintes.

Houve registros de chuva intensa nos bairros Caiçara e Camargos, em Belo Horizonte, e em Contagem. Segundo balanço do TRE-MG divulgado às 16h do domingo, 349 locais de votação no estado chegaram a ficar sem energia elétrica , mas as urnas continuaram funcionando com baterias próprias.

articles.title: Conheça os bispos que conduziram Igreja Católica em Rio Branco | G1
articles.standfirst: Dom Antônio Fontinele toma posse neste domingo (1º), em Rio Branco, e será o 6º religioso a conduzir instituição desde criação da Prelazia Acre-Purus, em 1920.
articles.summary: Dom Antônio Fontinele toma posse neste domingo (1º), em Rio Branco, e será o 6º religioso a conduzir instituição desde criação da Prelazia Acre-Purus, em 1920.
articles.body:
História da Diocese de Rio Branco escrita por seis bispos, de Dom Próspero M. Bernardi a Dom Antônio Fontinele, empossado neste domingo (1º) — Foto: Reprodução/Diocese de Rio Branco

A história da Igreja Católica no Acre atravessa mais de um século e passa pela atuação de cinco bispos que conduziram a instituição em diferentes momentos da formação religiosa e social do estado.

O capítulo mais recente começa neste domingo (1º), quando Dom Antônio Fontinele de Melo toma posse como novo o sexto bispo da Diocese de Rio Branco , em uma solenidade religiosa na Catedral Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, no Centro da capital, a partir das 8h.

Dom Antônio foi nomeado pelo Papa Leão XIV em 18 de setembro e será o sexto religioso a assumir a condução da Igreja Católica na região desde a criação da Prelazia Acre-Purus, em 1920.

Antes dele, passaram pela instituição Dom Próspero M. Bernardi, Dom Júlio Mattioli, Dom Giocondo M. Grotti, Dom Moacyr Grechi e Dom Joaquín Pertíñez, que renunciou em 1º de julho deste ano . Cada um teve participação em momentos importantes, desde as primeiras missões religiosas nos seringais até a organização da diocese e a ampliação de trabalhos sociais e pastorais.

A presença da Igreja Católica na região começou antes mesmo da criação da prelazia, que possui status semelhante ao de uma diocese. Com a chegada de nordestinos em busca da borracha, a partir de 1877, a religiosidade era mantida principalmente por meio de orações e devoções populares .

Naquele período, o território ainda pertencia à Bolívia e estava ligado à estrutura religiosa da Diocese de Manaus, por meio da paróquia de Lábrea, no Amazonas.

Em 1920, o papa Bento XV criou a Prelazia Acre-Purus e nomeou Dom Próspero M. Bernardi como primeiro bispo prelado. Integrante da Ordem dos Servos de Maria, ele iniciou os trabalhos missionários na região ao lado de outros religiosos.

As atividades incluíam visitas aos seringais, atendimento às comunidades mais distantes e a realização das primeiras Santas Missões Populares. Dom Próspero permaneceu à frente da prelazia até 1944.

Catedral Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, no Centro de Rio Branco, será local ocorre posse de Dom Antônio Fontinele — Foto: Diocese de Rio Branco

Depois de um intervalo de quatro anos, Dom Júlio Mattioli assumiu a condução da instituição, em 1948.

Durante os 14 anos em que esteve à frente da prelazia, Dom Júlio deu continuidade à criação de obras sociais, incentivou a abertura de novas paróquias e capelas e criou uma escola apostólica para acolher interessados na vida religiosa.

Um dos marcos de sua gestão foi o início da construção da Catedral Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, em Rio Branco, inaugurada em 1958.

Concílio Vaticano II e mudanças na Igreja

Entre 1965 e 1971, a prelazia foi conduzida por Dom Giocondo M. Grotti . Ele foi o primeiro e único bispo da Prelazia Acre-Purus a participar do Concílio Vaticano II, realizado entre 1962 e 1965, em Roma.

O encontro estabeleceu mudanças importantes nas diretrizes e práticas da Igreja Católica em todo o mundo. No Acre, Dom Giocondo iniciou a adaptação da prelazia às novas orientações, convocou a primeira Assembleia Geral e deu início aos trabalhos das primeiras pastorais e à construção de novas paróquias.

A Catedral Nossa Senhora de Nazaré , inaugurada durante a gestão anterior, também passou a fazer parte dos momentos históricos da instituição. O templo testemunhou a posse de Dom Giocondo e, posteriormente, de Dom Moacyr Grechi.

Dom Moacyr Grechi, quarto bispo da Diocese de Rio Branco — Foto: Reprodução

Dom Moacyr Grechi esteve à frente da instituição entre 1973 e 1998 . Foi durante sua gestão que ocorreu a transição da Prelazia Acre-Purus para a Diocese de Rio Branco , consolidando uma nova etapa da organização da Igreja Católica no estado.

Entre as principais iniciativas do religioso estiveram a criação da Pastoral da Juventude e da Pastoral Indigenista , a formação de agentes pastorais e a reorganização de paróquias e comunidades em cinco regiões pastorais.

O período também foi marcado pela atuação da Igreja em questões sociais. Dom Moacyr promoveu movimentos em defesa dos direitos dos indígenas, estudantes, professores e outras categorias profissionais, em um contexto de conflitos de terra e violência no Acre. Em 1998, ele deixou a Diocese de Rio Branco após ser nomeado arcebispo de Porto Velho, em Rondônia.

Dom Joaquín Pertíñez foi o mais longevo bispo da Diocese de Rio Branco — Foto: Richard Lauriano / Rede Amazônica

Dom Joaquín ficou 27 anos à frente da diocese

Em 1999, Dom Joaquín Pertíñez assumiu a Diocese de Rio Branco. O religioso permaneceu no cargo até 2026, completando 27 anos à frente da instituição. Durante sua gestão, foram criadas a Escola Diaconal e novas pastorais, além da reorganização de paróquias e comunidades.

Joaquín também promoveu Santas Missões Populares, criou e ampliou obras sociais e incentivou cursos de formação bíblica e missionária. Outro trabalho desenvolvido ao longo do período foi a formação de novos padres diocesanos.

A saída de Dom Joaquín ocorreu após um pedido de renúncia motivado por problemas de saúde , aceito pelo Papa Leão XIV em 1º de julho deste ano. Ele passou a ser bispo emérito.

Após a renúncia de Dom Joaquín, Dom Antônio Fontinele de Melo assumiu a administração apostólica da Diocese de Rio Branco em 12 de julho . Na época, ele ainda era bispo titular da Diocese de Humaitá, no Amazonas, e ficou responsável pela condução da instituição acreana durante o período de transição.

Mais de dois meses depois, em 18 de setembro, o Papa Leão XIV o nomeou oficialmente como novo bispo de Rio Branco . Com a decisão, Dom Antônio deixa a diocese amazonense para assumir definitivamente a Igreja Católica na capital acreana.

Nascido em 9 de maio de 1968, em Camocim, no Ceará, ele foi ordenado diácono em novembro de 1998 e padre em setembro de 1999. Antes de ser nomeado bispo de Humaitá, em 2020, atuou em diferentes funções na Arquidiocese de Porto Velho, incluindo como pároco, coordenador de pastoral e professor de Teologia.

A nomeação foi saudada pela Conferência Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB), que destacou a nova missão do religioso no Acre e agradeceu os seis anos de trabalho à frente da Diocese de Humaitá.

Dom Antônio Fontinele de Melo é oficialmente empossado neste domingo (1º) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A escolha da Catedral Nossa Senhora de Nazaré para a solenidade deste domingo tem um significado que vai além da estrutura física da igreja. O templo é considerado a igreja-mãe da diocese e representa simbolicamente a unidade das comunidades católicas que integram a instituição.

Segundo o padre Manoel, reitor da catedral, é justamente por esse simbolismo que a posse de um novo bispo ocorre nesse espaço.

“A catedral tem um simbolismo muito importante no conjunto da diocese. Para a gente fazer uma comparação, um corpo sem uma cabeça é uma coisa anormal. Uma diocese sem uma catedral é uma coisa acéfala. Então não tem cabeça. O bispo representa a cabeça da diocese. É simbólico e natural que a posse, o dia que ele toma possessão dessa igreja particular, seja na igreja catedral”, explicou.

A organização também prepara uma estrutura na área externa, com tendas e um telão para os fiéis que não conseguirem acompanhar a solenidade dentro da igreja.

“Todos os padres, freiras, seminaristas, diáconos, paróquias, comunidades [estarão presentes]. Então será um dia festivo. Será montado um grande telão lá fora, junto às tendas, com uma estrutura para acolher os fiéis”, afirmou o padre.

articles.title: Saga Leapmotor Uberlândia é premiada e apresenta SUV com até 900 km de autonomia | G1
articles.standfirst: Concessionária reconhecida no Melhores 2026 Top 100 amplia a mobilidade eletrificada na cidade e leva a tecnologia REEV, já presente no C10, ao B10 Ultra-Híbrido
articles.summary: Concessionária reconhecida no Melhores 2026 Top 100 amplia a mobilidade eletrificada na cidade e leva a tecnologia REEV, já presente no C10, ao B10 Ultra-Híbrido
articles.body:
B10 Ultra-Híbrido combina tração elétrica com motor a combustão usado como gerador — Foto: Divulgação/Leapmotor

A mobilidade eletrificada vem ampliando sua presença no mercado automotivo brasileiro, com opções que atendem a diferentes rotinas e necessidades de deslocamento. Em Uberlândia, a Saga Leapmotor Uberlândia participa desse movimento e recebeu reconhecimento na categoria Concessionária de Veículos Elétricos do Melhores 2026 Top 100.

A premiação destaca a atuação da unidade, instalada na Avenida João Naves de Ávila, 3.333, em um momento de expansão da marca na região. A operação local é conduzida pelo Grupo Saga e integra a estratégia da Leapmotor ao lado da Stellantis, grupo que reúne marcas já conhecidas do consumidor brasileiro e acrescenta credibilidade à chegada da fabricante ao país.

Entre as novidades está o B10 Ultra-Híbrido, SUV que utiliza um motor elétrico para movimentar as rodas e um motor a combustão para gerar energia. O modelo entra no mercado com preço competitivo em relação aos concorrentes, a partir de R$ 179.990, e com condições exclusivas de lançamento, que podem ser consultadas diretamente na concessionária. Segundo os dados divulgados para o modelo, a autonomia combinada pode chegar a 900 quilômetros no ciclo WLTP, dependendo das condições de utilização.

Reconhecimento local acompanha chegada de novas tecnologias

A Leapmotor iniciou sua operação comercial no Brasil em novembro de 2025. Em Uberlândia, a marca é representada pelo Grupo Saga, um dos grandes grupos de concessionárias do país, que passou a oferecer alternativas de eletrificação aos consumidores do Triângulo Mineiro.

O portfólio inclui os modelos C10 Elétrico, C10 Ultra-Híbrido e B10 Elétrico, que apresentam propostas distintas de uso. A tecnologia REEV já está presente no C10 Ultra-Híbrido, modelo que já tem praça em Uberlândia, e agora se expande com a chegada do B10 Ultra-Híbrido, ampliando as possibilidades para quem busca condução eletrificada com maior autonomia.

Nesse contexto, o reconhecimento no Melhores 2026 Top 100 acompanha a presença da concessionária no segmento e amplia a visibilidade das soluções de mobilidade eletrificada disponíveis na cidade.

Unidade de Uberlândia foi reconhecida na categoria Concessionária de Veículos Elétricos — Foto: Divulgação/Saga Leapmotor

O Leapmotor B10 Ultra-Híbrido utiliza a tecnologia REEV, sigla em inglês para veículo elétrico com extensor de autonomia. Nesse sistema, quem movimenta as rodas é o motor elétrico. O propulsor a gasolina não atua diretamente na tração: sua função é gerar eletricidade para alimentar o sistema e contribuir para a recarga da bateria.

A proposta é conciliar as características de condução de um automóvel elétrico com a possibilidade de percorrer trajetos mais longos sem depender exclusivamente da infraestrutura pública de recarga. Isso pode ser especialmente relevante em deslocamentos intermunicipais e regiões com poucos carregadores disponíveis.

De acordo com as informações técnicas apresentadas para a versão, o conjunto utiliza motor elétrico traseiro de 218 cavalos e 240 Nm de torque, bateria LFP de 18,8 kWh e motor 1.5 a gasolina empregado como gerador. O tanque de combustível tem capacidade de 50 litros.

A autonomia combinada anunciada é de até 900 quilômetros no ciclo WLTP, procedimento internacional de medição. O resultado real varia conforme velocidade, temperatura, relevo, carga transportada, uso de equipamentos e estilo de condução.

Na assistência ao motorista, o pacote ADAS de nível 2 reúne recursos como frenagem automática de emergência, reconhecimento de placas e controle de cruzeiro adaptativo. Essas tecnologias oferecem apoio em situações específicas, mas não tornam o automóvel autônomo: a atenção e a intervenção do condutor continuam indispensáveis.

O conjunto de segurança divulgado para a versão inclui sete airbags de série, entre eles uma bolsa central entre os bancos dianteiros, desenvolvida para reduzir o risco de contato entre os ocupantes em determinadas colisões laterais. A configuração também prevê tração traseira e suspensão independente, com sistema multibraço no eixo posterior. articles.title: Galeria subterrânea em Manaus: conheça o túnel histórico no Centro | G1
articles.standfirst: Espaço de cerca de 40 metros fica no subsolo do Centro Cultural Casarão de Ideias e guarda parte da história da capital. Visitação é gratuita, de quarta-feira a domingo.
articles.summary: A galeria subterrânea em Manaus, com 40 metros de extensão, fica no Casarão de Ideias e exibe relíquias da década de 1940 com entrada gratuita para o público.
articles.body:
Uma galeria subterrânea de aproximadamente 40 metros de comprimento guarda parte da história de Manaus . Conhecida como Galeria dos Ingleses, a estrutura fica no subsolo do Centro Cultural Casarão de Ideias, no Centro da capital , e pode ser visitada gratuitamente de quarta-feira a domingo, das 16h às 20h.

Em vídeo, o g1 mostra como é o interior da local centenário, descoberto este ano durante as obras de restauração do prédio onde funcionou a antiga Escola Estadual Saldanha Marinho. Assista acima .

Segundo João Fernandes, diretor do Casarão de Ideias, já havia relatos sobre a existência de um túnel no local, mas a estrutura só passou a ser explorada durante uma segunda etapa do projeto de restauração do prédio.

“Pra nós também foi uma surpresa, tanto quanto pra cidade. A gente já escutava falar, alguém ia no nosso inbox, dizia: ‘tem um túnel, tem um túnel’. Mas a gente resolveu fazer isso na segunda etapa. A primeira etapa a gente se dedicou ao prédio, a essa edificação. E depois a gente pensou: agora é o momento da gente conversar com a galeria”, explicou.

Para João Fernandes, a galeria representa um recorte da história da cidade e ajuda a compreender o processo de modernização de Manaus durante a Belle Époque, entre 1890 e 1920.

A galeria foi descoberta durante as obras de restauração do prédio que abriga o centro cultural. No local, funcionou a Escola Estadual Saldanha Marinho.

O corredor subterrâneo tem 40 metros de comprimento, dois metros de altura e dois metros de largura. A estrutura foi construída com tijolos cerâmicos maciços vermelhos, unidos por uma argamassa à base de cal e areia lavada.

Segundo o diretor, a mistura de cal e areia lavada ajudava a estrutura a resistir à força da água e à alta umidade do solo amazônico. A superfície interna lisa também reduzia o atrito da água e dificultava o acúmulo de resíduos.

Galeria subterrânea histórica escondida sob as ruas de Manaus será aberta ao público — Foto: Foto: Divulgação

Galeria desperta curiosidade dos visitantes

A existência de passagens subterrâneas no Centro de Manaus desperta a curiosidade de moradores e visitantes. Durante a entrevista, João Fernandes comentou sobre as histórias imaginadas pela população a respeito de possíveis ligações entre pontos históricos da capital.

“Eu acho que agora a cidade compreende um pouco da história que ela criou na cabeça dela. ‘Ah, e se eu entrar na galeria, no Teatro Amazonas, eu vou sair lá no porto?’. Com certeza sairia, né? E agora a gente mostra que isso em algum momento aconteceu”, comentou.

O diretor também destacou que algumas galerias da região da Avenida Eduardo Ribeiro continuam funcionando, enquanto outras foram desativadas.

Galeria subterrânea histórica escondida no Centro de Manaus tem objetos históricos. — Foto: Raimundo Cardoso/Rede Amazônica

A abertura do espaço atraiu visitantes, com filas para conhecer o túnel. Para João Fernandes, a procura demonstra o interesse da população pela história da capital e pelo acesso à cultura.

Além da estrutura, objetos encontrados durante o processo de restauração ajudam a contar a história do local. Entre eles estão antigas manilhas de barro, peças metálicas e garrafas da década de 1940, que também estão expostas aos visitantes.

🔎 Manilhas de barro: são tubos resistentes ao calor e à umidade, muito utilizados como chaminés para fogões a lenha, fornos e sistemas de esgoto ou drenagem.

articles.title: Pune woman found dead in flat rarely interacted with neighbours, told domestic help to stop coming for work: Cops
articles.summary: PUNE: A 34-year-old woman, who had secretly returned to India from the UK in August without informing her family, was found dead inside her Pune apartment
articles.body: PUNE: A 34-year-old woman, who had secretly returned to India from the UK in August without informing her family, was found dead inside her Pune apartment on Thursday.Before her death, Mugdha Deshmukh had told her domestic help that she was “leaving the flat” and asked her to stop coming for work, a police officer said.A native of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Deshmukh was found dead at a residential complex in the Gahunje area of Pimpri Chinchwad.Her family had been in touch with her through phone calls and messages. However, they were unable to reach her on October 24, after which her mobile phone was switched off, her father Avinash Deshmukh stated in a complaint lodged with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police earlier this week.The family subsequently contacted one of her friends in London, who said she had last communicated with Mugdha through messages on October 22.The friend approached London police to report her missing but was told that she had left the UK around the end of August, the officer said.Concerned about her whereabouts, the family sought assistance from Indian authorities and the Indian High Commission.Her father also examined her bank statements and noticed several transactions on food delivery and online service platforms between October 8 and 25, police said.One of the transactions was suspected to have originated from the Osmanpura area of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, leading the family to suspect that she might be in India.The family then approached the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar crime branch, expressing concern for her safety.Police traced her location to the Lodha Belmondo complex in Gahunje and alerted the Shirgaon police."The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police traced Mugdha's location to the Lodha Belmondo complex in Gahunje. We reached the flat she was residing in, gained entry with the help of a keymaker, and found her dead inside," said Chavan.Police said there were no visible injury marks on her body. articles.title: 'Twitchers gathered to see northern nutcracker on our gutter'
articles.summary: Teenager says "at least 50" cameras were pointed towards the house he was staying in.
articles.body:
Looking out of your window to find "at least 50" photographers staring back at you isn't the norm for many people.

But that's what teenager Max was faced with when a rare bird settled on the guttering of the Norfolk house he was staying in.

Max had come face to face with a flock of bird fans who had travelled from far and wide to Mundesley in the hope of spotting a northern nutcracker, not seen in the UK since 1991.

The 17-year-old said: "It was mad because all the photographers that were around in the street, it looked like they were all taking photos of us."

However, he said the confusion was brief as his grandfather eventually put two and two together.

Max, from Ruislip, West London, had already read about hundreds of twitchers causing disruption to buses in Mundesley after the bird was spotted in the area.

He said the bird stayed put for five to 10 minutes, flew off and then returned to settle outside their window.

The teenager said: "I don't know much about birds myself but it wasn't a very spectacular-looking bird.

"I didn't notice it was anything special but it was amazing because it was clearly a big deal for all these other people."

Northern nutcrackers are slightly smaller than a city pigeon but much chunkier and heavier than a blackbird.

A spokesperson for the RSPB said migrations like this are "not unheard of". They said pine seed crops in Siberia have likely failed, causing many birds to venture west in search of food.

Following the descent on the village by people hoping to see the bird, avid twitcher Wayne Glossop set up a fundraiser for Mundesley Inshore Lifeboat.

He said he wanted to "give something back" to the community. It has raised almost £1,500 so far, almost tripling its target.

articles.title: Rubio says Trump administration did not help Bolsonaro flee Brazil to US
articles.summary: Trump says defeated presidential candidate, who faces investigation in Brazil, can stay in the US ‘as long as he wants’.
articles.body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says President Donald Trump’s administration did not help Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro flee the country for the United States after losing a run-off to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

Bolsonaro arrived in Miami , Florida, on Wednesday, a day after the US Department of State said Bolsonaro and his family would be granted US visas after his October 25 election loss , which bucked a trend of conservative electoral wins in Latin America.

Bolsonaro is under investigation in Brazil for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion, and before leaving, he had been ordered to surrender his passport because police deemed him a flight risk.

“We didn’t facilitate anything,” Rubio told reporters on Saturday in Atlanta, Georgia, where diplomats from the Group of 20 largest world economies were gathered.

“We had word that he had arrived in the United States. He had previously held a visa, and the president made a decision to allow him to enter the country,” Rubio said.

He added that the US government was not “involved directly in any of the moves that were made”.

Rubio also said he had seen Brazil’s foreign minister, Mauro Vieira, in Atlanta on Friday and Saturday and he expected to see Brazilian officials again in November in France during a foreign ministers meeting.

Separately, Trump, who had previously called Brazil’s election “rigged” , voiced sympathy for Bolsonaro and said he could stay in the US indefinitely.

“I think he got treated very shabbily, very shabbily, so he can stay here as long as he wants,” the president told reporters at his Florida residence on Saturday.

The Reuters news agency reported that Bolsonaro was admitted to the US under humanitarian parole, a status that typically lasts for one year.

Trump’s comments suggested relations between the Western Hemisphere’s two largest democracies may remain strained for some time.

After Bolsonaro’s run-off loss, he fled Brazil to the US via Argentina and Ecuador on a journey that some US media outlets reported was partly arranged with the help of Jason Miller, a White House official.

Bolsonaro has refused to concede the Brazilian election and called the results fraudulent without providing evidence.

Since arriving in the US, he has claimed to be the true “leader” of Brazil and said he left the country because he was a victim of “persecution”.

articles.title: Armagh Observatory and Planetarium: 'Rok' solid recognition for space scientist
articles.summary: Two men from the Armagh Planetarium and Observatory have had asteroids named in their honour in recognition of their work.
articles.body:
As a child growing up in Slovenia in 1999, Dr Rok Nežič couldn't have known that an asteroid that was discovered in New Mexico that year would be named after him almost three decades later.

The Orchard County may be best known for its apples, but for Nežič the real attraction was astronomy.

He first arrived to Armagh Observatory and Planetarium (AOP) in 2015 to complete his doctorate in space and climate physics, and has remained there ever since.

More than a decade on, he is one of two AOP employees to have recently been chosen to have a celestial body named after them.

Nežič, who works at the planetarium as a tours and outreach officer, said he thought it was "so cool" when he learned that asteroids can be named after people.

Speaking to BBC News NI, Nežič said he wished he "could get there some day" and, now that he has, he described it as "a dream come true".

"I'm not sure how to believe it myself,” he admitted.

He explains that an asteroid is "a smallish rock in space" compared to planets, and that his one is named (20560) Nežič.

"That's its official name, so the number there tells you basically the order of discovery."

It is currently "sitting safely out in the asteroid belt and just going around the Sun, just like we are", he explained.

The naming process for small bodies in the solar system is governed by the International Astronomical Union . Asteroids can be named by their discoverers once their orbits are sufficiently known.

Nežič's asteroid is 10.9km across, while that belonging to his colleague Shane Kelly is 15.6km.

"They're both actually quite large as far as these asteroids that are named after people tend to be, because most of the really large ones were discovered first," Nežič said.

"So they were named a long time ago, and now we're finding smaller and smaller ones."

Nežič's asteroid was discovered by "one of the big missions", he said.

"This is an Earth-based mission in this case, which is looking for lots of asteroids, essentially, because the more we know about them, the more we know where they're going, the more we know which ones are not hitting us, including mine and Shane's."

To be considered for an asteroid namesake, someone must nominate you, and in Nežič's case, two people put his name forward.

He doesn't know who chose him for the honour - but his PhD supervisor, and a former astronomer from the observatory nominated him.

Nežič focused on comets with polarised light for his studies and years later is "still" talking about space.

The planetarium and observatory is "punching well above our weight", he said.

"Even though we're a small institution, people who work here can just focus on the research so much that we have really top researchers in the field."

The planetarium's neighbouring observatory has monitored the weather for more than than 230 years.

Shane Kelly, who is the principal meteorological observer at Armagh Observatory, was nominated by the emeritus director.

Since 1999, his role involves opening what is known as the Stevenson screen which holds sensitive thermometers, before noting down his readings for the day into the handwritten ledger.

His hand has entered far more lines of data than any of his 17 predecessors and his asteroid is called (7050) Shanekelly.

Kelly has been "doing this for 27 years", the institute's director said.

"He's probably observed the weather more than anyone else in the world, I suspect," Prof Michael Burton said.

"So this is in recognition of Shane's contribution to the observatory and to the measuring of the weather."

Kelly's asteroid was discovered in Chile in 1982.

Burton said it's "fantastic" that the two members of the team have been awarded in this way.

"There are now 29 asteroids which have some connection with the observatory and planetarium here in Armagh."

The AOP now plans on recognising their achievements with a new LED dome, which will show the asteroids and their orbits.

articles.title: Police storm Portugal housing protest camp
articles.summary: Dozens of officers, some accompanied by police dogs, moved into Rossio Square in Lisbon early on Sunday.
articles.body:
Police have used shields and batons to disperse housing protesters from a tent camp in Portugal’s capital, Lisbon, a week after similar operations drew criticism from protesters and rights groups.

Dozens of officers, some accompanied by police dogs, moved into Rossio Square at about 4:30am (04:30 GMT) on Sunday, a day after thousands marched demanding the government withdraw a rental bill they say would deepen the country’s housing crisis.

Protesters had erected more than 50 tents following Saturday’s march through Lisbon. Police commander Iuri Rodrigues issued three warnings to remove the tents, saying they had been erected illegally and that anyone resisting their removal could face disobedience charges.

Hundreds of demonstrators shielding the camp were dispersed, while police also dismantled a smaller encampment in Porto’s Dom Joao I square.

Earlier, lawmaker Pedro Delgado Alves said Rossio Square was peaceful and that nothing justified “a police intervention involving force, physical violence or baton charges, the kind of scenes we witnessed last week”.

The intervention followed operations in the same squares the previous Sunday, when police arrested 25 people in Lisbon and six in Porto. Housing campaign group Casa para Viver said 60 people were injured across those operations, which police described as “proportionate”.

The protests reflect growing anger over housing costs across Europe, including demonstrations in Spain and opposition to government economic policies in France, Germany and Albania.

Portugal faces one of Europe’s severest housing affordability crises, with young people among the hardest hit. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents on new leases have almost doubled.

The Bank of Portugal estimates a nationwide shortage of 300,000 homes, equivalent to Lisbon’s entire housing stock.

Demonstrators want the minority centre-right government to scrap legislation that would make evictions easier and remove rent caps on new leases, saying it would worsen affordability and leave tenants more exposed.

articles.title: Charities ask people to look out for hedgehogs after Storm Austen
articles.summary: Islanders are asked to take steps to prevent hedgehogs getting burnt in bonfires.
articles.body:
Wildlife charities have asked people to consider hedgehogs before disposing of any debris from Storm Austen in bonfires.

Animal welfare groups in both Guernsey and Jersey said more people may be planning to have bonfires after the storm brought down trees and branches . It comes as hedgehogs numbers have plummeted in the Channel Islands as the animals struggle to survive in hot summers.

Jersey Hedgehog Preservation Group advised people to build a bonfire on the day and not several days in advance as it "only takes one night for a hedgehog to move in".

Steve Byrne from the GSPCA in Guernsey advised people to check their bonfire carefully before setting light to it.

Gill Morgan, from the Jersey group, said: "Given that there will be plenty of raw material from the aftermath of the storm and the weather is due to improve over the next week people may be planning to get rid of their broken branches, twigs and leaves by burning them.

"Hedgehogs will be venturing out looking for food after the bad weather, and this is the sort of habitat they love to curl up in during the day."

The GSPCA has cared for 7,000 hedgehog since 2011.

Byrne said: "The winter weather causes challenges for our prickly friends so popping out water and food can really help them and with many thinking about bonfires next week we all need to help our hedgehog friends."

Byrne also advised people to check areas carefully before mowing or strimming, ensure netting is kept at a height that allows hedgehogs to pass safely under and check compost heaps before digging into them.

He also urged people to avoid using pesticides and poisons in their garden, to cover drains or deep holes and ensure there was an easy route out of ponds and pools for hedgehogs.

Guernsey Hedgehog Rescue Centre has previously reported a "steep" decline in numbers, while Jersey Hedgehog Preservation Group in St Helier has also reported a sharp drop.

The Jersey group said it had never had a casualty brought in after bonfire night but feared the animals would have been "killed outright and not rescued".

It said hedgehog numbers were in decline all over Europe, so any hazards that could be prevented would help their numbers recover.

Dru Burdon, another member of the group, said hedgehogs were under constant threat and would have struggled to raise their young this summer.

"With the very hot dry summers we have had the last three years, they have really been finding life difficult," said Burdon.

"Food has become very scarce just when they are trying to breed and increase their numbers again."

articles.title: Drivers urged to slow down after seven red squirrels hurt in a day
articles.summary: The JSPCA says it has been called to rescue seven squirrels injured on the roads in one day.
articles.body:
An animal shelter has issued a plea to drivers to slow down in woodland areas after seven red squirrels were injured on an island's roads in one day.

The JSPCA Animals' Shelter, in St Helier, Jersey, said that it had been called to a worrying number of casualties in "a short space of time".

Jersey has a thriving red squirrel population , due to the absence of grey squirrels, which carry a virus deadly to their red cousins.

Red squirrels are endangered in the UK , with about 120,000 to 160,000 left in the wild.

A post on the shelter's Facebook page urged drivers to reduce their speed when driving through areas where squirrels may be crossing and to keep an extra lookout, particularly near wooded areas and roads surrounded by trees.

If you hit a squirrel, the shelter have advised islanders to stop somewhere safe and either call the JSPCA for advice or bring the squirrel directly to them if it is safe to do so.

"These little animals are precious, and every life matters," the shelter said.

"A few extra seconds of care and attention behind the wheel could make all the difference.

"The little squirrel pictured escaped with just a split lip, which was expertly stitched back together by our wonderful JSPCA vets."

articles.body: Iran has linked the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to a series of demands from the United States, proposing a two-day timeline for restoring access to the strategic waterway as diplomatic talks involving Qatar continue, Al Jazeera reported.Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions with Qatari mediators had shortened the proposed implementation period from five days to two. However, the plan is conditional on Washington meeting Tehran's demands.“The Qatari side proposed shortening the implementation period of the Iranian proposal to five days. We have reached a proposal at this stage that reduces the implementation period to two days,” Araghchi said, news agency ANI cites.Iran's conditions include lifting US sanctions imposed after the Islamabad memorandum, reducing American military forces in the region, restoring oil waivers and releasing frozen Iranian funds, including those held in Qatar.Tehran has also demanded recognition of a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, established through discussions with Oman, and the closure of other routes.Araghchi said reopening the waterway on Iran's terms could pave the way for negotiations with Washington on outstanding issues.Iran insists on seven conditions for talksIran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei had earlier said negotiations would not take place and the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until Tehran's seven conditions were fulfilled.In a post on X, Rezaei said diplomacy remained possible if the US met Iran's demands but warned of retaliation if the country faced another attack.“We have repeatedly stated: the seven conditions announced by Iran must be fulfilled. If the conditions are met, the path of diplomacy will be open,” he said.Iran's demands also include ending the war across all fronts, particularly Israeli attacks on Lebanon.The latest developments follow the delivery of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Rezaei through Qatari mediators. articles.title: Hundreds fill Diwali food hampers in Birmingham to bring hope
articles.summary: The Diwali Basket Brigade volunteers want to help vulnerable households with rising food prices.
articles.body:
Hundreds of volunteers have packed food parcels to distribute to people across Birmingham struggling with the rising cost of living.

About 300 people turned up to the Diwali Basket Brigade event at the RSRS Centre in Hockley, which was organised by The Diwali Foundation.

It is the ninth time the charity has brought community volunteers from a variety of backgrounds together to make hampers in the build up to the religious festival.

Deepak Parekh, founder of the initiative, said: "[The] cost of living crisis hasn't gone away... but Diwali is a celebration of light over darkness, and this is our little way of bringing some light and some hope into the families that need it most."

The Diwali Foundation, who are based in Herefordshire, said that more than 12% of UK households are experiencing food poverty.

It works with about forty different food banks and charities to reach vulnerable households.

To date, the charity said it has provided around 23,470 food hampers to those in need.

Volunteer Clare Hannah said, while packing bags: "You're thinking about, 'oh I wonder what they're going to make with this'. And the fact that this is all that they've got, for some people."

Parcels were taken from Hockley to residents living in homes provided by Walsall Housing Group (whg).

Faye Shanahan from whg said: "It's really tough out there. Our customers are having a really hard time. The cost of living is not easing.

"Events like this today are really, really fantastic. It makes an absolutely fantastic difference to our customers."

Resident John Whiting, who turned 80 on Saturday, described his parcel as "unbelievable".

"There are a lot of people out there that've got nothing," he added.

"The food will be tremendous, thank you."

A London event was also held on Saturday, with similar events in Manchester and Leicester planned for Sunday.

Organisers have set a target of providing 6,000 food hampers this year, which would top a 2025 record when more than 80,000 meals were provided.

articles.title: Hampshire couple sue over 170 footballs landing in their £2 million garden; High Court awards £1,000 but allows school pitch to remain open
articles.summary: A Hampshire couple who complained that footballs repeatedly landed in their garden from a neighbouring school have been awarded £1,000 in damages, but the
articles.body: A Hampshire couple who complained that footballs repeatedly landed in their garden from a neighbouring school have been awarded £1,000 in damages, but the High Court has refused to shut down the facility. Mohamed and Marie-Anne Bakhaty brought a claim against Hampshire County Council after around 170 footballs entered their garden over 11 months. The balls came from the all-weather pitch at Westgate All Through School in Winchester. Judge Philip Glen ruled that footballs frequently crossing the boundary fence amounted to a nuisance, although the use of the pitch itself did not constitute an actionable nuisance.Why did a court rule against a school over garden nuisanceHigh Court Judge Philip Glen, sitting in Southampton, ruled that the frequent projection of footballs over the boundary fence constituted a nuisance. However, he distinguished this from the use of the all-weather play area itself, which he found did not give rise to an actionable nuisance. The ruling therefore recognised the couple’s complaint about footballs entering their property without prohibiting the school from continuing to use the pitch.In his written judgment, Judge Glen said he recognised that the couple were “extremely fond and proud” of their home, describing it as “on any view a beautiful home”. He also expressed concern that their response to the dispute had become disproportionate, stating that they had “become sensitised by the noise from the school” and were “over-invested in their belief that they are victims of a wrong”. He concluded: “In short, they have lost perspective.”Why did a court award £1,000 in a school pitch nuisance caseThe judge ordered Hampshire County Council to pay the Bakhatys £1,000 in damages in circumstances involving “excess use” of the play area and “significant numbers of balls” crossing the boundary fence. The award reflected the nuisance associated with footballs repeatedly entering the couple’s property, rather than a finding that the school’s entire playing facility was unlawful.Judge Glen also found that the noise from the school, whether or not the all-weather play area was in use, was “substantial, in the sense of not being trivial or transient”. He was satisfied that a substantial number of footballs had crossed the boundary before measures were introduced in 2022. The ruling did not, however, establish that the school had to stop using the pitch to resolve the dispute.How did a school try to stop footballs entering a couple’s gardenThe all-weather play area was built in 2021 and sits parallel to the boundary of the Bakhatys’ property, approximately 2 metres (6.6 feet) from their home. The couple’s property has a large garden and a swimming pool, and the garden is separated from the school facility by a wooden fence measuring 1.8 metres (5.9 feet) high.The school’s headteacher had written to the couple offering several measures to address their concerns. These included fencing off part of the area to create a buffer zone, installing a ball net and restricting use of the facility at certain times of the day. According to the BBC, the couple did not respond to the offer, but the school proceeded with measures to address the problem.Why did a court reject a ban on the school’s football pitchDespite finding that footballs crossing the property boundary amounted to a nuisance, Judge Glen refused to grant an injunction preventing the use of the all-weather play area. An injunction would have restricted the school’s ability to use the facility, but the judge did not consider such an order necessary in the circumstances of the case.The judge also indicated that a net could provide a practical way to prevent footballs and other objects from entering the neighbouring property. He said: “If a net was erected to prevent balls and other objects from crossing the boundary fence, I cannot necessarily see that there could be any real objection to opening this area up altogether.” He further stated that he did not consider that the council “threatens and intends” to “continue the nuisance”.What did the court rule in the Hampshire couple’s £1,000 garden disputeThe judgment left the school able to continue using its all-weather play area, while recognising the nuisance caused by footballs repeatedly crossing into the neighbouring garden. The court’s decision focused on the distinction between the use of the facility and the consequences of balls leaving the school grounds.The case resulted in a £1,000 damages award for Mohamed and Marie-Anne Bakhaty, but no order closing the pitch or prohibiting its use. The ruling also highlighted the importance of measures designed to prevent footballs from crossing property boundaries, with the judge identifying netting as a possible means of allowing the school facility to remain open while addressing the specific source of the dispute.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mamdani says Trump to grant visa to mother of boy killed in Bronx shooting
articles.summary: New York City mayor says US president ‘has agreed to grant her visa immediately’.
articles.body:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani says after a phone call with United States President Donald Trump that the mother of a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was shot dead in the Bronx will be granted a visa.

Mamdani wrote in a post on X on Saturday that he had spoken with Trump about Javits Frimpong, whose mother is seeking to travel to New York to say goodbye to her son.

The US president “has agreed to grant her visa immediately”, the mayor wrote.

“The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away,” he wrote.

There was no immediate comment from Trump.

CCTV footage that captured the last moments of Frimpong’s life showed him being chased by three other teens on Thursday morning as he was on his way to school. He was shot in his abdomen and died the same day in hospital. Thousands of people attended vigils held for the teenager across the city.

The 15-year-old had told his father he was bullied at school. Thomas Frimpong, Javits’s father, called on the police to help him “find justice for my son”. Police have said they are investigating, but no arrests have been made yet.

Javits’s parents moved him to the US a year ago in the hopes of providing him a better life. Congressman Richie Torres, who represents the Bronx, wrote on social media that “our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him.”

Ghanaian Foreign Minister Sam Okudzeto Ablakwa stated on social media that Ghanaian officials are “coordinating with local authorities” and helping Javits’s mother with her visa application. Visa applications from a number of African countries have been severely limited under the Trump administration.

articles.title: 'Why do you challenge democracy?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of acting on behest of foreign powers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of acting at the behest of foreign powers, alleging that the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of acting at the behest of foreign powers, alleging that the opposition was attempting to create instability and challenge an elected government under the pretext of defending democracy.Addressing the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) march in Haryana’s Rohtak, Nabin said the party's campaign was aimed at countering what he described as a deliberate attempt to spread chaos across the country.Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) president Jayant Chaudhary was also present on the stage.“As we participate in this 'Save Democracy' march, we must address the atmosphere of chaos and instability that is being deliberately spread throughout the nation,” Nabin said.He alleged that Rahul Gandhi was working to further the agendas of foreign powers and seeking to challenge India's democratic system at their direction.“They are the same purveyors of chaos who have recently been sowing discord abroad. Their associates, members of the Communist Party and certain Congress leaders, talk about 'changing the regime.' But this is a government formed by the mandate of the people; no one can even lay a finger on it,” he said.Nabin also questioned the Congress's criticism of electoral outcomes, arguing that the party accepted democratic mandates when it won elections but raised concerns over the electoral process when it lost.“You (Congress) have no faith in the country’s 1.4 billion people. In whom, then, do you place your trust? In 3 crore infiltrators! I ask you, Rahul Gandhi: what exactly is your intention? Why do you challenge democracy?” he said.Citing electoral outcomes in different states, Nabin said the Congress described democracy as having prevailed when it won in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka, but claimed it was under threat after losing in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.He further accused the Congress of seeking to run the country according to the wishes of the Gandhi family, saying that governance should instead be guided by the Constitution.Nabin challenges opposition on voter deletion claimsBJP president also targeted the Congress over its allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls and criticism of the Election Commission of India (ECI).Referring to the 1975 Allahabad High Court judgment that set aside then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli, Nabin accused the Congress of having a history of misusing government machinery during elections.“When Indira Gandhi won an election, the Allahabad High Court ruled that she had won by misusing the entire govt machinery and employing improper means. Her election was completely annulled, and she was barred from contesting elections for six years,” he said.He also challenged Rahul Gandhi's claims regarding the deletion of 13 crore votes, saying the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance (NDA) partners were prepared to provide details of the deletions.“Today, they claim that 13 crore votes have been deleted. I say to you, Rahul Gandhi, that any worker from our party, the NDA, or even one of our local unit presidents can provide a detailed account for every single one of those 13 crore deleted votes,” Nabin said.He added that the BJP was willing to discuss the issue either in public or in Parliament. Nabin also accused the Congress of seeking to protect infiltrators and said BJP and NDA workers would work to ensure their removal from the country.BJP leader raises 1984 anti-Sikh riots, targets Gandhi familyNabin also criticised the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, arguing that the party should have apologised for the violence instead of taking part in protests on the issue of electoral integrity.He referred to former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's remark after the assassination of Indira Gandhi that “when a big tree falls, the earth shakes”, saying it should have prompted remorse from the Congress leadership.“When our Sikh brethren were being slaughtered, when a full-scale massacre was unfolding, your father remarked that 'when a big tree falls, the earth shakes.' Because of that 'shaking of the earth,' the lives of so many of my Sikh brothers were extinguished. You should have felt remorse for this; you should have apologised,” he said.The BJP president also accused the Congress of practising dynastic politics and alleged that its leaders followed the directions of the Gandhi family rather than democratic principles.His remarks came as the INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' march from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday.The opposition alliance is protesting against alleged irregularities in electoral rolls during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had alleged that shops in Connaught Place were forcibly shut ahead of the march, causing losses to local traders. In a post on X, he said the opposition had encouraged rally participants to shop in the area but found commercial establishments closed.The BJP also organised a separate march in West Delhi to remember the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of holding its political rally on the anniversary of the violence.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland
articles.summary: Officers received 144 fireworks-related calls on Saturday night - down on 160 on 31 October last year.
articles.body:
Police Scotland received 144 fireworks-related calls on Saturday night - down on 160 on 31 October last year.

Fireworks were thrown at people, buildings and vehicles in some parts of Scotland on Halloween.

Officers said in general there was "outstanding behaviour and co-operation" around the country but were working to identify to those responsible for disorder.

Firework Control Zones (FCZs) - where it is an offence to set off fireworks - are in place in 14 areas in Edinburgh and four in Glasgow until early November, and dispersal zones are in force in some places.

On Halloween there were reports of fireworks lit in the street and some thrown at members of the public in Glasgow, Tranent in East Lothian and Bonnyrigg in Midlothian.

Police said no officers were injured and inquiries to identify those involved were ongoing.

Operation Moonbeam, which runs up to the evening of 5 November, means police can call on specially trained officers to deal with violence and disorder.

It is the annual police response to firework-linked criminality, which is now in its ninth year.

This year, FCZs banning the use of pyrotechnics in certain areas run from 30 October to 8 November in Edinburgh and until 9 November in Glasgow.

Seven dispersal orders were also issued in Edinburgh and work was ongoing to establish the number issued in Glasgow that relate to Operation Moonbeam.

Ch Supt David Robertson said: "The overwhelming majority of Scotland's communities have celebrated Halloween in the proper spirit and I'm really grateful for the support of our efforts tonight to deter criminality, respond to reports of disorder and protect the public and emergency services from harm.

"Sadly, however, we have again experienced incidents of fireworks used as projectiles at buildings, vehicles and members of the public.

"This type of behaviour is completely unacceptable and has to stop before there are serious consequences."

He said investigations would be launched immediately and Operation Moonbeam officers would continue to support local policing teams on fireworks-related crime over the next week.

articles.title: A mother says her Doberman kept crying and refusing to leave her six-month-old son; doctors later found the baby's heart was racing at 280 beats per minute and diagnosed a rare electrical condition
articles.summary: A pet Doberman's unusual behaviour around a six-month-old baby in England led his mother to seek medical help, after which doctors discovered that the
articles.body: A pet Doberman's unusual behaviour around a six-month-old baby in England led his mother to seek medical help, after which doctors discovered that the child had a dangerously fast heartbeat of 280 beats per minute. The incident happened in September when Kim Reynolds, 41, from Shepton Mallet in Somerset, noticed that her dog, Saraya, was repeatedly crying and refusing to leave her son Alexander alone, SWNS reported. Doctors later diagnosed the baby with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, a condition that affects the electrical signals controlling the heartbeat.Kim, a first-time mother and former canine hydrotherapist, was familiar with dogs but had never seen Saraya behave this way around Alexander. The Doberman appeared unusually concerned about the baby and became upset whenever he was moved away from her. At first, Kim could not understand what was troubling the animal.Later that day, Alexander began showing signs of illness, so she took him to the emergency department at Royal Bournemouth Hospital.By the time they reached the hospital, Alexander had stopped crying. Kim wondered whether the visit had been necessary. However, when doctors examined him, they found that his heart was beating at 280 beats per minute and the baby needed immediate treatment to bring his heart rhythm under control.Baby's heartbeat remains high Doctors first attempted to slow Alexander's heartbeat using cold water and ice. Kim recalled that medical staff placed her son in a container of icy water as part of the procedure. She found the experience distressing, particularly when she heard him scream.The treatment was attempted twice, but Alexander's heartbeat remained unusually fast. According to Kim's account, his head was submerged for around 10 seconds during the procedure. When the attempts failed, he was returned to her lap.Kim then asked whether doctors could use medication instead. Alexander was given medicine intravenously, and his heart rate eventually came down after three doses.Once his condition had been stabilised, he was taken by ambulance to Poole Hospital for further care. Kim remained in hospital with her son for two nights while doctors investigated what had caused his heartbeat to become so fast.Two days after the first emergency visit, Alexander was diagnosed with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.What causes Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome?According to MedBound Times, Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, also called WPW syndrome, is a congenital heart condition that involves an extra electrical connection between the heart's upper and lower chambers.Normally, electrical signals travel through the heart along a controlled pathway, helping maintain a regular heartbeat. In people with WPW syndrome, the additional connection can allow signals to travel differently, sometimes triggering episodes in which the heart beats much faster than normal.These episodes can involve supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), a condition in which the heartbeat becomes abnormally fast. In young children, warning signs can include breathing difficulties, pale skin, irritability and restlessness.Doctors commonly use an electrocardiogram, or ECG, to identify WPW syndrome. The test records the heart's electrical activity. Other investigations, including heart monitoring and an echocardiogram, may also be recommended depending on the patient's symptoms.Alexander now receives propranolol, a beta-blocker used to help control his heart rate. Kim gives him the medicine three times daily through a syringe. She says he has become comfortable taking it and does not resist the treatment.Dog's behaviour raises concern againThe September hospital visit was not the only occasion when Saraya's actions made Kim worry about Alexander's health.Later that month, the baby was sitting in his bouncer when the Doberman began behaving unusually again. Saraya stayed close to him, licked his hands and repeatedly looked towards Kim.Remembering what had happened earlier, Kim immediately wondered whether Alexander was experiencing another episode of SVT. She checked his pulse but also noticed that his throat looked red.Kim decided to take him to hospital again. This time, doctors found that he had bacterial tonsillitis rather than another reported episode of his heart condition. Alexander was prescribed penicillin.Saraya has not received specialist training to identify medical conditions and is not registered as an assistance dog. Nevertheless, Kim says the two incidents have made her pay close attention whenever the Doberman behaves differently around her son.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces seize strategic positions in al-Jawf
articles.summary: Weapons and ammunition depots are seized after a counteroffensive.
articles.body:
Yemen’s internationally recognised government says its forces have recaptured military positions and strategic heights east of al-Hazm, the capital of the northern governorate of al-Jawf, while fighting continues to deepen the humanitarian crisis in the besieged city of Taiz.

The army’s media centre said in a post on X on Saturday that the 1st Emergency Brigade seized weapons and ammunition depots after wounding, killing and capturing Houthi fighters. It also said the attacks resulted in the destruction of armoured vehicles.

The Houthis, meanwhile, said they had thwarted advances by government forces in al-Jawf and neighbouring Marib.

Al-Jawf borders Saudi Arabia and lies alongside the Houthi-held governorates of Sanaa and Saada, making it a vital strategic front in the government’s campaign to regain territory. The fighting is part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, launched in October to reverse Houthi gains and restore government control over territory held by the group, which seized Sanaa in 2014.

Fighting has also continued around Taiz in southern Yemen with government forces saying they repelled Houthi attacks in al-Aqroudh, southeast of the city, and on the Tur al-Baha front in neighbouring Lahij governorate.

Meanwhile, Houthi-affiliated media reported that two air strikes targeted an oil company facility in Bajil district in Hodeidah governorate.

The fighting comes as the siege of Taiz strains hospitals and restricts deliveries of food, fuel and medical supplies. Although the Houthis do not control the city, they hold key routes in and out of it, limiting access to essential supplies and making it harder for civilians to leave amid reported sniper fire from the surrounding hillsides.

Videos published by Yemeni media showed what the outlets described as the first shipment of medical aid arriving from Marib to support wounded people, displaced families and other residents. Further shipments were reportedly held up by road closures.

More than 290,000 people have fled their homes since fighting escalated in August, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. The UN Population Fund said nearly 6,100 pregnant women were among those recently displaced, including 600 expected to give birth within two weeks of its briefing on Friday.

The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees warned that more than 65,000 refugees and asylum seekers in Yemen face worsening conditions as services are disrupted and food and fuel prices rise.

articles.title: Northern Lights dance across UK sky on Halloween night
articles.summary: Stargazers across the UK were treated to the vivid colours of the aurora borealis on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Stargazers around the UK were treated to the vivid colours of the aurora borealis on Saturday night.

As cloud and rain on the weather front cleared southwards, parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland were perfectly placed to catch the display.

The eerie glow provided a fitting finale to spookiest night of the year, delighting skywatchers and photographers alike.

Aurora activity may continue into Sunday night, especially in northern skies, but the display is likely to be less intense than the one seen on Halloween night.

Where to look for the aurora on Sunday night

The Northern Lights might well be visible again on Sunday night but mainly in Scotland, Northern Ireland and Northern England.

According to the Met Office Space Weather Centre, following a recent increase in solar wind activity, there is another chance of seeing the Northern Lights tonight, particularly across northern Scotland.

However, a weather front moving into the far north may bring increasing cloud, potentially obscuring views in some areas.

Where skies remain clear, the aurora could still put on a display, although activity is expected to be less intense than on Halloween night and should gradually ease from Monday onwards.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday warned Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah that they would face legal action over alleged vote theft, saying they would be next after Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Addressing the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, Rahul said the opposition would pursue action against those allegedly involved in manipulating elections. articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from Washington: For all the attention that the 2026 midterm elections in the US are attracting over control of the House, Senate, and
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: For all the attention that the 2026 midterm elections in the US are attracting over control of the House, Senate, and governorships, a municipal contest in California with strong political and electoral ties to India is challenging the Golden State -- and America’s -- reputation as a bastion of capitalism.The Mayoral election in Los Angeles, whose $ 15 billion budget matches that of Costa Rica or Chhattisgarh, pits incumbent Karen Bass, 73, against Nithya Raman, 45, an India-born socialist councilwoman whose challenge has turned into one of the more intriguing political contests of the election season. Polls show the race currently tied, with Bass, a Democrat backed by the establishment, including California Governor Gavin Newsom, Kamala Harris, and Nancy Pelosi, clawing back from a ten-point deficit in September.If however Raman wins on Nov 3, LA will join New York City, now led by Zohran Mamdani, in having a mayor of Indian ancestry identified with democratic socialism. It would underscore the irony of two of America's most economically powerful, globally influential and famously expensive cities being governed by politicians from a movement that Trump and his political allies routinely portray as an existential threat to American capitalism.Raman's story has a typical Indian middle class template. Born in Kerala, she moved to the U.S at the age of six and grew up in Louisiana and Massachusetts, going to become an accomplished urban planner after graduating from Harvard and MIT. She moved back to India in 2009, establishing Transparent Chennai, an urban research and advocacy initiative, and worked on sanitation and water access in the city. Returning to LA in 2013, she became involved in neighborhood activism, particularly around homelessness anf affordability. She is married to Vali Chandrasekaran, a Hollywood tv screenwriter, whose credits include episodes for hit sitcoms 30 Rock and Modern Family.In 2020, Raman defeated an incumbent to become the first Indian elected to the LA City Council and went on to build a reputation for activism on affordable housing, tenant protections, and climate policy, eventually identifying herself as a Democratic Socialist. Her Mayoral campaign centers around a simple proposition: LA is a spectacularly wealthy city that is somehow lousy at providing basic services to its residents. She promises more affordable housing, better public infrastructure and a more accountable homelessness program, pointing to a nearly 50% reduction in street homelessness in her council district, even as the city's overall numbers have increased -- a jab at Bass whose term is dogged by rising living costs, infrastructure gridlock and persistent homelessness in the City of Angels.There is, incidentally, an interesting Indian historical footnote to LA’s -- and for that matter California’s and America’s -- flirtation with socialism. Long before Mamdani and Raman began making their mark in American municipal politics, several prominent Indian nationalists and intellectuals had encountered the country's radical political traditions first hand.Lala Lajpat Rai spent five years in the U.S between 1914 and 1919, establishing the India Home Rule League and publishing the journal Young India in New York. The radical humanist MN Roy arrived in the US in 1916 as a global itinerant, encountered American radicals and began studying socialism, subsequently moving to Mexico City, where he founded the Communist Party of Mexico in 1919. He later played a foundational role in establishing the Communist Party of India in 1920.B.R. Ambedkar, meanwhile, studied at Columbia University in NYC, encountering some of America's leading liberal and progressive intellectuals, including philosopher John Dewey. And Jayaprakash Narayan spent seven years in America (1922-1929), studying at Berkeley, Iowa, and Wisconsin, where he encountered Marxism and returned to India a committed socialist.All this was at a time socialism was enjoying considerable electoral popularity. In 1912, Socialist Party presidential candidate Eugene Debs won nearly a million votes, then about 6% of the national total. Socialists also held hundreds of municipal offices, including mayoralties. In fact, in the early 1950s Donald Trump’s father Fred Trump clashed with the folk singer Woody Guthrie, an avowed socialist, over racial segregation and housing discrimination in Brooklyn, causing him to write a song -- a scalding takedown of a predatory landlord -- titled “Old Man Trump" who stirred up racial hatred "in the bloodsport of the human heart."The subsequent “Red Scare” and the association of socialism with communism marginalized the movement, but almost a century later “the times they are a-changing.” Of course, Mamdani and Raman represent a different generation and a more modern version of democratic socialism. Neither is proposing to abolish private property or install a Soviet-style command economy; their politics revolve around housing affordability, public services, redistribution, workers' rights and making the wealthy contribute more towards the common good.For Trump, who has made fighting socialism a defining feature of his political identity, the prospect of New York and Los Angeles being governed by two such politicians, that too of “foreign” origin, might be particularly galling. For India, meanwhile, there is something deliciously ironic about the possibility that two of America's most influential cities could be led by activists with Indian roots, carrying forward a political tradition that some of India's own intellectual giants first encountered on American soil.You use AI every day. articles.title: 16-year-old girl goes to meet boyfriend, 'gangraped' by driver, 2 others in Jharkhand
articles.summary: MEDININAGAR: A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gangraped in Jharkhand's Palamu district, a senior police officer said on Sunday.
articles.body: MEDININAGAR: A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gangraped in Jharkhand's Palamu district, a senior police officer said on Sunday.Three people have been arrested in connection with the case, he added.The incident occurred on October 29 in the Untari Road police station area when the girl was returning home in an e-rickshaw, police said."The minor had gone to meet her boyfriend after learning that his parents had fixed his marriage with someone else. Upon reaching there, she could not meet him. While returning, the driver of the vehicle and two others took her to a secluded place and raped her," Palamu SP Kapil Choudhary told news agency PTI.Police arrested the three accused, aged between 20 and 38, on October 31 after registering an FIR based on the girl's statement, he said.The accused have been booked under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act."The girl's medical examination has been conducted and her condition is stable. Further investigation into the case is underway," another officer said.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)(With agency inputs)Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
