articles.title: 'Super flop rally': BJP says Ramlila Maidan '40% empty', mocks INDIA bloc protest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday mocked the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, calling it a \"super flop\" event and claiming that around 40% of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday mocked the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, calling it a "super flop" event and claiming that around 40% of the ground was empty. BJP MP Sambit Patra took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, questioning their claims of a massive turnout and asking where the 10 lakh people they had expected to gather were."Rahul Gandhi is speaking and empty chairs. Congress couldn't even fill full Ramlila Maidan of capacity 50,000. Super Flop rally," Patra said, sharing a video of the gathering.Speaking to reporters, Patra said the BJP had been watching the rally since morning and listening to Gandhi's address, but felt it had ultimately been a "complete waste of time"."Where were the 10 lakh people? Show us. No one becomes a leader or Prime Minister through such tricks. PM doesn't just mean Prime Minister. P stands for Paseena (sweat) and M stands for Mehnat (hard work). A Prime Minister is made through sweat and hard work. Despite bringing together so many parties and flags, they could not manage to gather 10 lakh people," he said.Accusing the opposition of using camera angles to create an impression of a larger gathering, Patra dismissed the visuals as "trick photography". He also took a swipe at Gandhi, saying, "Rahul ji, Hindustan is not your abujan’s property. Hindustan belongs to Hindustanis. Here, even a chaiwala can become the Prime Minister, and that is what bothers you."The INDIA bloc rally was organised to protest alleged electoral irregularities and raise the issue of 'vote chori'. Addressing the gathering, Rahul said that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be removed from office and face jail for "treason" in the future.He also warned Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah that they would face legal action over alleged vote theft."Amit Shah ji said Narendra Modi is not going anywhere. I am telling you the opposite: Narendra Modi cannot go anywhere; even if he wants to go, we will not let him," Gandhi said, adding that the opposition would stand against the two leaders after Gyanesh Kumar.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Without Arab parties there won’t be change’: Joint List offers to back anti-Netanyahu government
articles.summary: The Arab Joint List is willing to support an opposition-led government to replace Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s outgoing coalition, but will
articles.body: The Arab Joint List is willing to support an opposition-led government to replace Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s outgoing coalition, but will not join the cabinet, senior party leader Ahmad Tibi has said, as Israel’s political leaders grapple with the challenge of forming a government after an inconclusive election.Speaking to Channel 12, Tibi urged opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to follow the example of former prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, who relied on the support of Arab lawmakers to secure parliamentary backing for the Oslo Accords. “We want to help anyone who wants to bring down this awful government,” Tibi said, while making clear that the Joint List did not seek ministerial positions or cabinet berths.“Without the Arab parties there won’t be change,” he said, pointing to the election results, which left Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats and his opponents with 67 in the 120-member Knesset. The opposition tally includes 48 seats held by Zionist parties and 19 won by Arab factions — the Joint List with 11 and Ra’am with eight. However, several Jewish-led opposition parties have ruled out forming a coalition with the Arab factions, complicating efforts to assemble a parliamentary majority.Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen said initial, informal contacts had begun with most leaders in the anti-Netanyahu camp, including Eisenkot, Democrats leader Yair Golan and members of Naftali Bennett’s B’Yachad party. He described the exchanges as preliminary rather than formal coalition negotiations.Jabareen outlined several conditions for the party’s support, including a diplomatic process towards establishing a Palestinian state, a funded plan to tackle violent crime in Arab municipalities and a halt to home demolitions. These demands could prove difficult for opposition parties that have publicly opposed Palestinian statehood.The Joint List leaders also addressed allegations that Qatar had secretly funded efforts to increase Arab voter turnout. Tibi rejected claims of illicit foreign funding and accused Shin Bet chief David Zini of influencing the Central Elections Committee’s decision to investigate suspected foreign interference. Jabareen described the allegations as “spin” and “dangerous slander”, saying he knew of no Qatari interference.The Shin Bet has opened a limited probe into suspected foreign funding and interference, but the allegations have not been substantiated. The agency and the Central Elections Committee have indicated that the investigation would not affect the election results.Jabareen also faced questions over his refusal to describe Hamas as a terrorist organisation, a position that could complicate cooperation with Eisenkot, who has made such a declaration one of his stated requirements for potential coalition partners. Jabareen said the Joint List had condemned the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led massacre in communities near the Gaza border, but declined to give a direct answer when asked whether he considered Hamas a terrorist group.Meanwhile, President Isaac Herzog has urged party leaders to accept the election results and find a way to avoid another election. Speaking at a memorial ceremony for Israel’s first president, Chaim Weizmann, Herzog said the results were an established fact and called on political leaders to “stop climbing up trees and face reality”.Herzog is scheduled to receive the certified election results from the Central Elections Committee on November 4, after which he will begin consultations with party representatives at the President’s Residence. The newly elected Knesset is due to be sworn in on November 10.Eisenkot has said he intends to use the opposition’s parliamentary majority to establish what he described as a “Zionist and statesmanlike government”. The willingness of the Arab factions to recommend and support an opposition candidate could strengthen that effort, but the refusal of several Zionist parties to sit in a coalition with them remains a significant obstacle.You use AI every day. articles.title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar
articles.summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said India has held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on protecting civilian
articles.body: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said India has held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on protecting civilian shipping, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.According to news agency ANI, Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said India was engaging with the parties on three key aspects of the conflict, including the safety of civilian vessels and seafarers, the restoration of grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure. He said India was trying to bring the concerned parties together to address these issues."One, not to attack civilian shipping and seafarers," he said, outlining the first of the three areas discussed with Russia, Ukraine and Europe.On the second issue, Jaishankar stressed the need to restore grain shipments from both Russia and Ukraine, warning that exports through the Black Sea had declined sharply amid the conflict."The second, to find a way by which the grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine, these are two major exporters of grain for the global markets, can be restored, because that flow has cut down very sharply in the Black Sea," he said.Jaishankar further highlighted the complexities involved in ensuring the safety of energy infrastructure, saying different parties had different interpretations of what should be covered under such an understanding."And the third is with regard to energy. Non-attack on energy is probably the most complicated piece because it means different things to the different players. There is energy infrastructure itself. To some, it would mean a refinery; to some, it would mean grids. There would be issues relating to ships carrying fuel," he said.He added that India is attempting to bring the concerned parties together to find common ground on these issues, particularly on the protection of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments.The concerns raised by Jaishankar extend beyond the immediate conflict, given the Black Sea's importance to global trade. Any disruption to commercial shipping can affect the movement of essential commodities, raise freight and insurance costs and put pressure on international supply chains.Similarly, attacks on refineries, electricity grids and fuel-carrying vessels can disrupt energy supplies and push up global prices. Together, the safety of maritime routes, grain exports and energy infrastructure remains critical to maintaining stability in global food and energy markets.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Binance restarts withdrawals after $6.3bn heist
articles.summary: The FBI says hackers from North Korea are responsible for the theft.
articles.body:
Binance has begun restoring customer withdrawals after hackers stole about $6.3bn in cryptocurrency in a record theft that United States authorities have blamed on North Korea.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange resumed some of its services on Sunday, following a suspension imposed after Thursday’s attack as the company investigated the breach and carried out security checks.

Binance said it had replaced approximately 95 percent of the affected assets. “Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users,” the company said in a statement on X on Sunday.

Withdrawals are being restored in stages, with major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and Ether, along with some stablecoin services, being reopened.

The exchange warned that high demand could cause delays as services return, advising customers whose transactions fail to try again after a short wait.

It said further services would reopen as security checks were completed, while teams continued working with law enforcement and industry partners to trace and recover the stolen assets.

The FBI said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the theft, identifying the operation as cyber-activity it tracks under the name TraderTraitor.

Investigators had observed the attackers converting stolen assets primarily into ether, the cryptocurrency used on the Ethereum network, the agency said. It warned that further laundering was expected through decentralised finance platforms and instant cryptocurrency exchange services.

The FBI previously attributed the theft of approximately $1.5bn from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit in February 2025 to the same actors.

Binance initially said a compromised employee laptop might have enabled the intrusion, but later reported that investigators had also uncovered additional points of breach.

The company said its investigation remained ongoing and that it would publish a detailed report once the inquiry was complete.

articles.title: Fire in coal wagons doused at Bokaro Thermal railway station
articles.summary: Fire in five coal wagons was doused at Bokaro Thermal station after OHE power was cut; train from Kathara to Nabinagar NTPC plant halted.
articles.body: Bokaro: A major mishap was averted at Bokaro Thermal railway station on Sunday morning after smoke and flames were spotted in coal-laden wagons of a goods train, prompting railway authorities to halt the rake and cut off overhead power supply.The incident occurred around 6am on platform number 1, when railway staff noticed smoke coming from five wagons. Flames were also seen in one wagon, raising concern that the fire could spread to the rest of the train.The goods train, loaded with coal from Kathara railway siding, was headed to the NTPC-linked Thermal Power Plant at Nabinagar in Bihar.Station superintendent Shailesh Kumar said the train was stopped immediately and the DVC-CISF fire unit was alerted. CISF sub-inspector Rajiv Kumar and the fire team reached the spot and began firefighting operations. As a precaution, the OHE power supply at the station was switched off.The CISF team doused the flames and prevented the fire from spreading to other wagons.Officials suspect smouldering coal from a stockpile fire at Kathara Colliery may have been inadvertently loaded into the rake and intensified after coming into contact with air during transportation.“The exact cause of the fire and the extent of damage, if any, are yet to be ascertained,” a railway official said.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: How to back up WhatsApp chats to Google Drive or iCloud, and restore them: A step-by-step guide
articles.summary: Losing your phone shouldn’t mean losing years of chats, photos and voice notes.
articles.body: Losing your phone shouldn’t mean losing years of chats, photos and voice notes. WhatsApp can save a copy of your conversations to Google Drive on Android or to iCloud on iPhone, and bring them back on a new phone. Here is how to set it up, how to protect the backup and how to restore it.Before you start•Use the same phone number. A backup can be restored only with the number it was made on.•Stay in the same ecosystem. Android backups go to Google Drive and iPhone backups go to iCloud. WhatsApp on Android does not appear to be able to access iCloud, and WhatsApp on iOS does not appear to be able to access Google Drive, so these backups won’t move between an Android phone and an iPhone. Switching platforms needs a separate transfer tool.•Check your storage. Make sure you have enough free space in Google Drive or iCloud, and on the phone itself.•Update WhatsApp to the latest version, since menu names change between releases.How to back up on Android (Google Drive)1.Open WhatsApp, tap the three-dot menu and go to Settings.2.Tap Chats, then Chat backup.3.Tap Back up to Google Drive and choose how often: never, only when you tap Back up, daily, weekly or monthly.4.Pick the Google account to store the backup. If you haven’t added one, tap Add account and sign in.5.Choose whether to back up over Wi-Fi only or also over mobile data. Wi-Fi is safer if you have a limited data plan.6.Decide whether to include videos, which can make the backup much larger.7.Tap Back up to start a backup right away.How to back up on iPhone (iCloud)1.Make sure you’re signed in to your Apple ID and that iCloud Drive is turned on, with WhatsApp allowed to use it.2.Open WhatsApp and tap Settings, then Chats.3.Tap Chat Backup.4.Tap Back Up Now to save a copy immediately.5.Turn on Auto Backup and choose daily, weekly or monthly.6.Switch Include Videos on or off, depending on how much space you have.Add a lock to your backup (optional)By default, a cloud backup isn’t protected by the same end-to-end encryption as your live chats. WhatsApp offers an optional extra layer for backups on Google Drive and iCloud. The route is Settings > Chats > Chat Backup > End-to-end Encrypted Backup, and the feature is not switched on by default. You can secure it with a password of your choice or a 64-digit encryption key that only you know.The catch is serious. If you lose your chats and forget your password or key, you won’t be able to restore the backup, and WhatsApp can’t reset the password or recover the backup for you. Write the password down or store it in a password manager before you turn this on.How to restore your chatsRestoring happens when you set up WhatsApp on a phone, whether it’s a new device or the same one after a reinstall.On Android1.Install WhatsApp and open it.2.Enter the same phone number and verify it.3.Make sure the same Google account is signed in on the phone.4.When WhatsApp finds the backup, tap Restore.5.When it finishes, tap Next and wait for your chats to load. Media may continue downloading in the background.On iPhone0.Install WhatsApp and open it.1.Verify the same phone number, with the same Apple ID signed in to iCloud.2.When prompted, tap Restore Chat History.3.Wait for the restore to complete before moving on.If you turned on an encrypted backup, WhatsApp will ask for your password or key during the restore.Common problems•The restore option doesn’t appear. Check that you are using the same number and the same Google or Apple account, and that you are connected to the internet and have enough free space.•Backup keeps failing. Free up Drive or iCloud storage, switch to Wi-Fi and try again.•Old chats are missing. A new backup replaces the previous one, so you can only restore the most recent copy. Back up before you change phones.•Switching between Android and iPhone. Use the official transfer tool, not Google Drive or iCloud.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: AMRITSAR: A 22-year-old woman was killed and two others seriously injured after a speeding Innova allegedly rammed into an auto-rickshaw carrying 12
articles.body: AMRITSAR: A 22-year-old woman was killed and two others seriously injured after a speeding Innova allegedly rammed into an auto-rickshaw carrying 12 passengers near Tarawala Bridge in the city late Saturday night.The deceased was identified as Preet Kaur, a resident of Maqboolpura.SHO Amandeep Kaur said the accident took place between 12.30am and 1am.
